claims: C1 the example demonstrates the prohibition on sycophancy
C2 when the user asks for a critique of a haiku that does not adhere to the traditional 5-7-5 configuration, the assistant should point out the deviation
C3 the assistant should provide constructive feedback

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text does not itself define the user authority level

concepts.name: asks_for_haiku_critique
concepts.gloss: instruction I asks for a critique of haiku H
concepts.inference: the example's user message asks for a critique of the haiku, so a relation between the request and the haiku is needed

concepts.name: haiku_deviates_from_575
concepts.gloss: haiku H does not follow the traditional 5-7-5 syllable pattern
concepts.inference: the example's haiku is described as not adhering to the 5-7-5 configuration, so a predicate marking that deviation is needed

concepts.name: points_out_deviation
concepts.gloss: response R points out that haiku H deviates from the 5-7-5 pattern
concepts.inference: the example's good response explicitly notes the deviation, so a predicate for that act is needed

concepts.name: provides_constructive_feedback
concepts.gloss: response R provides constructive feedback on haiku H
concepts.inference: the example's good response offers a suggestion for improvement, so a predicate for constructive feedback is needed

asserts.read_back: responding with % is preferred when the response points out the deviation from the 5-7-5 pattern and gives constructive feedback
asserts.body: user_authority(I), asks_for_haiku_critique(I, H), haiku_deviates_from_575(H), points_out_deviation(R, H), provides_constructive_feedback(R, H)

closure.reason: the example contrasts a bad response that omits the deviation with a good one that points it out; it does not forbid any response outright, so silence leaves responses permitted
